captions.twitter:
Big numbers lie to your brain.

We turn them into pictures.

This is Wait, How Big? — one perspective shift a day.
captions.instagram:
Big numbers are hard to feel. We turn them into pictures. Follow for one perspective shift a day.

#visuallearning #dataviz #sciencecommunication
captions.tiktok: Big numbers are hard to feel. So we’re making them visible. Follow the 30-day experiment. #visuallearning #facts #scale

captions.twitter:
A million seconds is 11.6 days.
A billion seconds is 31.7 years.

Three extra zeros changed days into decades.
captions.instagram:
A million seconds: 11.6 days. A billion seconds: 31.7 years. Save this for the next time someone says “just add three zeros.”

#dataviz #mathfacts #visuallearning
captions.tiktok: Your brain hears “million” and “billion” as neighbors. They are not. Which comparison should we visualize next? #math #facts #scale

captions.twitter:
The Moon is not “right next to” Earth.

At the average distance, about 30 Earths fit in the gap.

Most diagrams compress space beyond recognition.
captions.instagram:
Most textbook diagrams compress this distance beyond recognition: about 30 Earths fit between Earth and Moon at the average gap.

Source: NASA Science
#spacefacts #visualscience #dataviz
captions.tiktok: The Moon looks close because diagrams cheat. The average gap can fit about 30 Earths. #space #nasa #scale

captions.twitter:
The Sun is about 100× wider than Earth.

But width is only one dimension.

By volume, about 1.3 million Earths fit inside it.
captions.instagram:
The Sun is roughly 100× wider than Earth, but volume grows in three dimensions. About 1.3 million Earths would fill its volume.

Source: NASA Science
#spacefacts #visuallearning #sciencecommunication
captions.tiktok: The Sun is about 100× wider than Earth—but volume grows in three dimensions. Result: ~1.3 million Earths. #space #science #scale

captions.twitter:
Drop Everest into Challenger Deep and its summit would still sit roughly 2.1 km underwater.

Tallest mountain above sea level: ~8.85 km
Deepest ocean point: ~10.94 km
captions.instagram:
Put Everest at Challenger Deep and the summit would remain about 2.1 km below the surface.

Depth source: NOAA Ocean Exploration
#oceanfacts #geography #visualscience
captions.tiktok: Everest is enormous. Challenger Deep is deeper. The summit would still be roughly 2.1 km underwater. #ocean #geography #scale

captions.twitter:
The Pacific Ocean is larger than all continental landmass combined.

It covers more than 155 million km².

Flat maps make that scale difficult to feel.
captions.instagram:
The Pacific Ocean covers more than 155 million km²—larger than all continental landmass combined.

Source: NOAA Ocean Exploration
#geographyfacts #oceanfacts #dataviz
captions.tiktok: One ocean is larger than all the continents combined. Maps make this surprisingly hard to feel. #geography #ocean #scale

captions.twitter:
Give every person on Earth exactly 1 m² of standing room.

8.2 billion people would form a square about 91 km on each side.

Important: standing room is not housing or a functioning city.
captions.instagram:
Thought experiment: give 8.2 billion people exactly 1 m² each. The resulting standing square is roughly 91 km per side. It says nothing about homes, roads, food, or infrastructure.

Population basis: UN World Population Prospects
#population #dataviz #visuallearning
captions.tiktok: At one square meter each, 8.2 billion people need a square about 91 km wide. This is standing space only—not a livable city. #population #math #scale

captions.twitter:
$1 billion in stacked $100 bills: ~0.69 mile.
$1 trillion: ~690 miles.

A trillion is not “a somewhat larger billion.” It is one thousand billions.
captions.instagram:
Using the U.S. Currency Education Program’s estimate of more than 14.5 million notes per mile: $1B in $100s stacks to ~0.69 mile; $1T stacks to ~690 miles.

#moneyfacts #dataviz #visuallearning
captions.tiktok: In $100 bills, a billion-dollar stack is under a mile. A trillion-dollar stack is roughly 690 miles. #money #math #scale

captions.twitter:
Compress Earth’s ~4.5-billion-year history into one calendar year.

Homo sapiens arrive on Dec 31 at about 11:25 PM.

Our entire species fits into the final ~35 minutes.
captions.instagram:
Earth’s history as one year: Homo sapiens arrive on December 31 at roughly 11:25 PM. The exact minute varies with the age estimates used; the point is the scale.

Sources: NASA Science; Smithsonian Human Origins
#deeptime #visualscience #history
captions.tiktok: If Earth’s 4.5-billion-year history were one year, our species appears only in the final ~35 minutes. #history #science #scale

captions.twitter:
Saturn and its main rings would fit between Earth and Moon.

Main-ring diameter: ~273,550 km
Average Earth–Moon gap: ~384,400 km

The diffuse outer E ring is excluded.
captions.instagram:
Yes: Saturn and its main rings would fit between Earth and Moon at the average gap. NASA notes that this excludes Saturn’s diffuse outer E ring.

#spacefacts #saturn #visualscience
captions.tiktok: Saturn plus its main rings would fit in the average Earth–Moon gap. The diffuse outer E ring is excluded. #saturn #space #scale

captions.twitter:
Earth’s longest mountain range is mostly underwater.

The mid-ocean ridge runs about 65,000 km—roughly 1.6 times around the equator.
captions.instagram:
The mid-ocean ridge stretches about 65,000 km—roughly 1.6 times around Earth at the equator.

Source: NOAA Ocean Exploration
#earthscience #oceanfacts #geography
captions.tiktok: The world’s longest mountain range is mostly invisible beneath the ocean: about 65,000 km long. #ocean #earthscience #scale

captions.twitter:
A blue whale can be longer than an NBA court.

Blue whale: up to roughly 100–110 ft
NBA court: 94 ft
captions.instagram:
Blue whales can reach roughly 100–110 feet. An NBA court is 94 feet long.

Sources: NOAA Fisheries; NBA Jr.
#bluewhale #animalfacts #visuallearning
captions.tiktok: The largest animal on Earth can be longer than an NBA court. #animals #ocean #scale

captions.twitter:
1 million hours ≈ 114 years.
1 billion hours ≈ 114,000 years.

Three extra zeros move from a lifetime into deep prehistory.
captions.instagram:
One million hours: about 114 years. One billion hours: about 114,000 years. Three zeros move the comparison from a lifetime to deep prehistory.

#mathfacts #dataviz #visuallearning
captions.tiktok: A million hours is 114 years. A billion hours is about 114,000 years. #time #math #scale
